title: Where Do AI Coding Agents Fail? An Empirical Study of Failed Agentic Pull Requests in GitHub
authors: Ramtin Ehsani; Sakshi Pathak; Shriya Rawal; Abdullah Al Mujahid; Mia Mohammad Imran; Preetha Chatterjee
central_claim: 33,596 AIDev-pop agent PRs (>100-star repos): 71.48% merged (open PRs count as not merged); logistic model: each additional failed check-run on the last commit lowers merge odds ~15% (coef -0.1579, OR 0.85); rejection taxonomy of 562 coded PRs: abandoned 228, duplicate 142, CI/test failure 99.
cite_claim: C21 (verified): 71.48% of 33,596 agent PRs merged; each failed CI check-run associated with ~15% lower merge odds. Cite as association, all-PR denominator.
location: Sec. 3 RQ1 (merge rates, Table 1 logistic regression); Sec. 2 (CI collection: last commit check-runs); Sec. 3 RQ2 Table 2 (taxonomy)
quote: Notably, each additional failed CI check decreases the odds of a merge by about 15%.
relevance: Primary basis of C21 and the CI-before-PR gate motivation; caveats: open PRs in denominator, Codex-dominated, CI at last commit, model spec unreported.

title: The Rise of AI Teammates in Software Engineering (SE) 3.0: How Autonomous Coding Agents Are Reshaping Software Engineering
authors: Hao Li; Haoxiang Zhang; Ahmed E. Hassan
central_claim: AIDev: 456,535 agent PRs, 61,453 repos, 47,303 developers (v1); AIDev-pop (500+ stars) 7,122 PRs; agent PR acceptance below humans; Codex accepted PRs median 0.3 h vs 3.9 h for humans.
cite_claim: Agent-authored PRs are accepted less often than human PRs in the same repos (Codex 64%, Devin 49%, Copilot 35%, humans 15-40 points higher, v1 snapshot).
location: Sec. 4.2; Table 5 (%Accepted: Human 76.8, Codex 65.3, Devin 48.9, Copilot 38.2, Cursor 51.4, Claude Code 52.5); Table 3
quote: OpenAI Codex PRs cut review time by 10 times, boosting efficiency but questioning review depth
relevance: Origin of the AIDev dataset used by C21 and all 2026 follow-ups; text and Table 5 rates disagree slightly.

title: AIDev dataset (Hugging Face dataset card)
authors: Hao Li et al. (SAIL, Queen's University)
central_claim: AIDev v4 has 2,743,854 agent PRs across 327,477 repos (cutoff Nov 2025, adds Google Jules); v5 (7.6M, cutoff 2026-03-31) in progress; CC-BY-4.0, source repos keep their licences.
cite_claim: Public, CC-BY-4.0 dataset on which C21-style acceptance statistics can be re-computed.
quote: AIDev-2.7M
relevance: Enables the HA3 re-analysis baseline (denominators, self-merge exclusion, multivariable CI model).

title: On the Use of Agentic Coding: An Empirical Study of Pull Requests on GitHub
authors: Miku Watanabe; Hao Li; Yutaro Kashiwa; Brittany Reid; Hajimu Iida; Ahmed E. Hassan
central_claim: 567 Claude Code PRs in 157 projects matched with 567 human PRs: 83.77% vs 91.00% merged (closed PRs only; 54 open excluded); 54.94% of merged agent PRs merged without further commits; 45.1% revised, mostly bug fixes.
cite_claim: C22 (verified): 83.8% of closed Claude Code PRs merged; 54.9% of those without modification; human PRs 91.0%.
location: Sec. 3 (identification: 'Generated with Claude Code'); Table 2; Sec. 4.3-4.4; Sec. 7.2 (survival bias)
quote: 475 of 567 merged, 83.77% acceptance [paraphrased table row; verify exact phrasing]
relevance: Reused claim C22; shows closed-only denominator and that reviewers often add tests/edge cases to agent PRs (16.4% of revised).

title: Do Autonomous Agents Contribute Test Code? A Study of Tests in Agentic Pull Requests (MSR'26 title: An Empirical Study of Tests in Agentic Pull Requests)
authors: Sabrina Haque; Sarvesh Ingale; Christoph Csallner
central_claim: In AIDev-pop closed PRs (31,284), test-inclusion rose 31%->52% over time; merge rates of test vs non-test PRs are similar for most agents (Claude 72.1 vs 70.6, Codex 85.2 vs 86.2, Copilot 56.8 vs 53.8, Cursor 71.6 vs 75.6) and lower for Devin (44.1 vs 60.6); test PRs take longer.
cite_claim: Including test code in agent PRs does not consistently raise merge rates (descriptive, no size controls).
quote: Devin is an exception, merging test-containing PRs less frequently than non-test PRs.
relevance: Counter-evidence for 'tests raise acceptance'; motivates the direct HA2 evidence ablation.

title: Human-Agent versus Human Pull Requests: A Testing-Focused Characterization and Comparison
authors: Roberto Milanese; Francesco Salzano; Angelica Spina; Antonio Vitale; Remo Pareschi; Fausto Fasano; Mattia Fazzini
central_claim: From AIDev v3 (932,791 agent PRs), 6,582 agent PRs and 3,122 human PRs (500+ stars, 4 languages): 42.9% vs 40.0% include tests (OR 1.13, p=0.008); test-detection heuristic F=0.985; acceptance not analysed.
cite_claim: Agent PRs include tests at a similar (slightly higher) rate than human PRs in the same popular repositories.
quote: 2,821 HAPRs (42.9%) and 1,248 HPRs (40.0%) contain test files [paraphrase of counts; verify wording]
relevance: Context for test-inclusion base rates; does not support an acceptance effect.

title: LGTM! Characteristics of Auto-Merged LLM-based Agentic PRs
authors: Ruben Branco; Paulo Canelas; Catarina Gamboa; Alcides Fonseca
central_claim: Many agent PRs are merged with no review; repositories auto-merge all or none of their agent PRs; auto-merged PRs are smaller; two repos make up 37.2% of AIDev-pop PRs; Codex and Claude Code have the highest auto-merge rates.
cite_claim: Pooled agent-PR merge rates are inflated by unreviewed auto-merges and a few dominant repositories; Codex acts under the user's credentials.
quote: We define Auto-Merge as merging a PR without reviews or review comments
relevance: Key denominator/self-merge caveat for C21; fiks PRs would face real review, unlike auto-merged agent PRs.

title: Why and When Agentic Pull Requests are (not) Accepted: An Exploratory Study
authors: Marius Christoph Strauss; Sandro Schulze
central_claim: Association rule mining on closed AIDev-pop PRs: base acceptance 79.89%; 84.1% of agent PRs closed within 60 min (vs 56.5% human); acceptance lift >1 only for PR age < 5 min; smaller PRs and fast responses co-occur with acceptance.
cite_claim: On closed PRs only, agent PR acceptance in AIDev-pop is ~80%, and acceptance concentrates in PRs closed within minutes.
location: Sec. 3.2 (open PRs removed); Sec. 4.1 Finding 1; Sec. 4.2 (PR age)
quote: Given that the regular acceptance rate is 79.89%
relevance: Shows denominator sensitivity of C21 (71.48% all vs 79.89% closed) and the self-merge signature.

title: When AI Teammates Meet Code Review: Collaboration Signals Shaping the Integration of Agent-Authored Pull Requests
authors: Costain Nachuma; Minhaz F. Zibran
central_claim: AIDev-pop 33,596 PRs: 71.5% merged, 21.6% closed unmerged, 6.9% open; reviewer engagement is the strongest correlate of merge; larger changes and force-pushes lower odds; touching test files has no significant independent effect.
cite_claim: Among agent PRs, reviewer engagement, not test inclusion, is the strongest correlate of integration.
quote: reviewer engagement has the strongest correlation with successful integration
relevance: Confirms open-PR share inside C21's denominator; null test effect.

title: Early-Stage Prediction of Review Effort in AI-Generated Pull Requests
authors: Dao Sy Duy Minh; Huynh Trung Kiet; Nguyen Lam Phu Quy; Pham Phu Hoa; Tran Chi Nguyen; Nguyen Dinh Ha Duong; Truong Bao Tran
central_claim: On 33,707 AIDev v1.0 agent PRs: 28.3% merge instantly (Codex 42.9% of its PRs vs Copilot 0.1%); acceptance 68.7% for non-instant PRs; size dominates review effort; CI-touch benefit disappears after controlling for agent identity.
cite_claim: A large share of agent PRs merge instantly (self-merge regime), and acceptance of PRs that actually get reviewed is lower.
location: Abstract; Sec. results (two-regime behaviour; ghosting; SHAP)
quote: excel at narrow automation (28.3% of PRs merge instantly)
relevance: Separates self-merged from reviewed agent PRs; the reviewed regime is the relevant prior for fiks.

title: Understanding Dominant Themes in Reviewing Agentic AI-authored Code
authors: Md. Asif Haider; Thomas Zimmermann
central_claim: 19,450 inline review comments on 3,177 agent PRs, 12 themes; beyond correctness, reviewers focus on documentation gaps, refactoring and style; testing and security also appear.
cite_claim: Reviewers of agent PRs spend much of their attention on documentation, refactoring and style, not only correctness.
quote: predominantly focus on documentation gaps, refactoring needs, styling and formatting issues
relevance: Suggests fiks PR quality (docs, minimal diff, style) matters beyond green tests; informs blind-review rubric.

title: How AI Coding Agents Communicate: A Study of Pull Request Description Characteristics and Human Review Responses
authors: Kan Watanabe; Rikuto Tsuchida; Takahiro Monno; Bin Huang; Kazuma Yamasaki; Youmei Fan; Kazumasa Shimari; Kenichi Matsumoto
central_claim: Agents have distinct PR-description styles associated with differences in reviewer engagement, response time and merge outcomes (abstract only read).
cite_claim: PR description style of coding agents is associated with reviewer engagement and merge outcomes [verify details in full text].
quote: exhibit distinct PR description styles
relevance: Supports testing the PR evidence block (HA2); full text not deep-read.

title: MSR 2026 Mining Challenge track (AIDev) - accepted papers
authors: MSR 2026 organisers
central_claim: AIDev is the MSR 2026 Mining Challenge dataset (932,791 agent PRs; curated 33,596 PRs from 2,807 >100-star repos); ~60 accepted papers incl. >=10 on agent PR acceptance/rejection and 5 on tests in agent PRs.
cite_claim: Agent-PR acceptance is an active 2026 research topic built on a single shared dataset (AIDev).
location: Track page: dataset description; Session 2 posters list
quote: 932,791 Agentic-PRs [as listed on track page; verify exact wording]
relevance: Index of follow-ups; flags that many conclusions share one dataset and its biases.

title: PR Arena: tracking PRs opened and merged by coding agents
authors: aavetis (GitHub)
central_claim: Live GitHub-search counts of agent PRs: 'ready PR' success rates Copilot 95.97%, Codex 90.24%, Jules 84.47%, Devin 64.63%, Codegen 62.24%, Cursor 101.66% (inconsistent); no as-of date shown.
cite_claim: Public agent-PR 'merge rate' trackers use non-comparable denominators (ready/non-draft PRs) and can report impossible values.
quote: This repo tracks the opened and merged PRs by the top SWE coding agents
relevance: Cautionary example: do not cite tracker numbers as maintainer acceptance.

title: Bots Don't Mind Waiting, Do They? Comparing the Interaction With Automatically and Manually Created Pull Requests
authors: Marvin Wyrich; Raoul Ghit; Tobias Haller; Christian Mueller
central_claim: 20,623,320 GitHub PRs (2019-01 to 2020-05, GHTorrent): human 13,770,280 PRs 72.53% merged vs bot 6,853,040 PRs (4,654 bots) 37.38% merged; bot PRs take longer to be interacted with and merged.
cite_claim: Bot-authored PRs are merged about half as often as human PRs (37.38% vs 72.53%, all PRs regardless of status).
quote: Total includes all PRs in the dataset ignoring their current status.
relevance: Unconditional base rate for a bot proposing a PR; the right prior for an unsolicited fiks PR.

title: Automating Dependency Updates in Practice: An Exploratory Study on GitHub Dependabot
authors: Runzhi He; Hao He; Yuxia Zhang; Minghui Zhou
central_claim: 1,823 projects, 502,752 regular Dependabot PRs: 70.13% merged, median merge lag 0.18 days; security PRs 73.71-76.01%; compatibility score <80% -> 30.20% merged, 95-99% -> 84.43%; 11.3% of projects deprecated Dependabot; noise and fatigue are key.
cite_claim: In adopting projects, >70% of bot dependency-update PRs are merged, and a machine-computed CI-based safety score strongly tracks merge rate (30.2% vs 84.4%).
location: Sec. 5.2 Table 5; Sec. 5.3 Table 6; Sec. 3 project selection
quote: if the score is lower than 80%, developers become very unlikely (30.20%) to merge
relevance: Closest published analogue to fiks attaching verifiable evidence to a bot PR; also sample-selection caveat (projects with >=10 merged Dependabot PRs).

title: Can automated pull requests encourage software developers to upgrade out-of-date dependencies?
authors: Samim Mirhosseini; Chris Parnin
venue_or_publisher: ASE 2017, pp. 84-94 (as cited by He et al. 2023) [primary not opened]
central_claim: Greenkeeper automated PRs: developers update 1.6x more often, but only 32% of Greenkeeper PRs are merged, due to update suspicion and notification fatigue.
cite_claim: Only 32% of Greenkeeper's automated PRs were merged [secondary via He et al. 2023, Sec. 2; verify in primary].
location: He et al. 2023, Sec. 2 Related Work (secondary)
quote: only 32% of Greenkeeper PRs are merged due to two major limitations
relevance: Classic bot-PR acceptance baseline and the trust/noise mechanisms fiks must avoid.

title: On the use of Dependabot security pull requests
authors: Mahmoud Alfadel; Diego Elias Costa; Emad Shihab; Mouafak Mkhallalati
venue_or_publisher: MSR 2021, pp. 254-265 (as cited by He et al. 2023) [primary not opened]
central_claim: Dependabot (Preview) security PRs: 65.42% merged, most within a day; security PRs take longer to close than merge.
cite_claim: 65.42% of Dependabot security PRs were merged, mostly within a day [secondary via He et al. 2023; verify primary].
location: Cited in He et al. 2023 (arXiv 2206.07230), Sec. 2 Related Work; primary MSR 2021 paper not opened [verify]
quote: 65.42% of PRs are merged and most are merged within a day
relevance: Security-fix bot PRs as a closer analogue to fiks fix PRs; URL is a placeholder to locate primary [verify].

title: About Dependabot security updates: compatibility scores
authors: GitHub
central_claim: Dependabot's compatibility score is the percentage of CI runs that passed for the same update in other public repositories.
cite_claim: Dependabot attaches a cross-repository CI pass rate to each update PR as evidence of safety.
quote: An update's compatibility score is the percentage of CI runs
relevance: Defines the evidence signal whose merge association He et al. measured; design precedent for fiks receipts in PRs.

title: The Power of Bots: Understanding Bots in OSS Projects
authors: Mairieli Wessel; Bruno Mendes de Souza; Igor Steinmacher; Igor S. Wiese; Ivanilton Polato; Ana Paula Chaves; Marco A. Gerosa
central_claim: 93 of 351 popular GitHub projects (26%) use bots; no consistent significant before/after differences in PR comments, commits, files or time to close; surveyed developers find bots not smart enough.
cite_claim: Bots are common in popular OSS projects, but adopting them showed no consistent change in PR outcomes.
quote: We sampled 351 popular projects from GitHub and found that 93 (26%) use bots.
relevance: Foundational bot-in-OSS study; tempers claims that a bot improves maintainer outcomes.

title: Don't Disturb Me: Challenges of Interacting with Software Bots on Open Source Software Projects
authors: Mairieli Wessel; Igor Wiese; Igor Steinmacher; Marco A. Gerosa
central_claim: Interviews with 21 practitioners: noise from bots on PRs is a recurrent, central problem that disrupts communication and workflow.
cite_claim: Noise is the central challenge of PR bots for maintainers.
quote: a recurrent and central problem
relevance: Motivates rate limits and grouping of fiks PRs (HA5).

title: Quality Gatekeepers: Investigating the Effects of Code Review Bots on Pull Request Activities
authors: Mairieli Wessel; Alexander Serebrenik; Igor Wiese; Igor Steinmacher; Marco A. Gerosa
venue_or_publisher: Empirical Software Engineering (ICSME 2020 special issue) [verify year]; arXiv 2103.13547
central_claim: Regression discontinuity on 1,194 projects plus 12 interviews: adopting a code-review bot increases monthly merged PRs, decreases non-merged PRs and decreases human communication.
cite_claim: Adopting an evidence-reporting (code-review) bot was followed by more merged and fewer non-merged PRs (RDD).
quote: increases the number of monthly merged pull requests
relevance: Quasi-causal evidence that machine-generated evidence on PRs can shift merge outcomes.

title: Human-competitive Patches in Automatic Program Repair with Repairnator
authors: Martin Monperrus; Simon Urli; Thomas Durieux; Matias Martinez; Benoit Baudry; Lionel Seinturier
central_claim: Repairnator produced 5 patches accepted and merged by human developers; Expedition 1 reproduced 3,551 of 11,523 failing builds and found 15 build-passing patches, none human-competitive; PRs were proposed under a human persona because developers are biased against bot contributions.
cite_claim: Repair bots driven by CI failures can get patches merged, but rarely (5 merged); bias against bot contributions led the authors to disguise the bot.
location: Sec. on human-competitiveness; Expedition #1 and #2; Table 1
quote: human engineers do not accept contributions from bots as easily as contributions from other humans
relevance: Closest prior to a repair bot opening PRs to outside maintainers; bot-identity bias risk for fiks.

title: Agentic Program Repair from Test Failures at Scale: A Neuro-symbolic approach with static analysis and test execution feedback
authors: Chandra Maddila et al. (Meta) [verify author list]
central_claim: Feb-Apr 2025: 1,589 diffs published, 1,285 reviewed, 405 landed (31.5% of reviewed, 25.5% of published); gates before review: failing test passes, LLM judge, CI; most common negative comment: test already fixed or flaky (47/100).
cite_claim: Of agent-generated fixes that received review at Meta, 31.5% were accepted; staleness/duplication was the top rejection reason.
location: Abstract; Table V; Sec. on engineer feedback
quote: Of those that received a review, 31.5% were accepted.
relevance: Industrial prior for acceptance of gated fix diffs; motivates a duplicate/already-fixed check (HA4).

title: Evaluating Agent-based Program Repair at Google
authors: Pat Rondon et al. (Google) [verify author list]
central_claim: Agent patches for machine- vs human-reported bugs: plausible 73% / 25.6% vs valid 43% / 17.9%; validity judged by three authors, not by merge.
cite_claim: Test-passing (plausible) patches overstate correctness; human validity review is needed to interpret repair success.
quote: We determine this correctness through manual analysis performed by three of the authors.
relevance: Rubric source for fiks blind review (G12); distinguishes validity from maintainer acceptance.

title: Automated Unit Test Improvement using Large Language Models at Meta
authors: Nadia Alshahwan; Jubin Chheda; Anastasia Finegenova; Beliz Gokkaya; Mark Harman; Inna Harper; Alexandru Marginean; Shubho Sengupta; Eddy Wang
central_claim: TestGen-LLM: 75% of generated tests built, 57% passed reliably, 25% increased coverage; 73% of its recommendations accepted by Meta engineers for production.
cite_claim: Filtered, verified LLM-generated tests were accepted by engineers 73% of the time at Meta.
quote: verifies that its generated test classes successfully clear a set of filters
relevance: Shows heavy pre-filtering plus additive changes yields high acceptance; contrasts with 31.5% for fix diffs.

title: Finding and fixing software bugs automatically with SapFix and Sapienz (Meta Engineering blog)
authors: Yue Jia; Ke Mao; Mark Harman (Meta Engineering) [verify]
central_claim: SapFix generates fixes for crashes found by Sapienz and requires engineer approval before deployment.
cite_claim: Industrial auto-repair keeps a mandatory human approval step.
location: Blog body (reused from catalog; verified by sibling areas)
quote: is not designed to deploy fixes to production code on its own
relevance: Precedent for fiks's never-merge policy.

title: Work Practices and Challenges in Pull-Based Development: The Integrator's Perspective
authors: Georgios Gousios; Andy Zaidman; Margaret-Anne Storey; Arie van Deursen
central_claim: Survey of 749 integrators: tests in a PR are a positive signal, CI success reinforces trust, 75% run tests via CI; contradicts earlier mining (Gousios 2014; Tsay 2014) where test inclusion was not a strong factor in acceptance or decision time.
cite_claim: Integrators state that tests and passing CI raise their trust in a contribution, although mining studies found test inclusion was not a strong acceptance factor.
location: Sec. on quality factors (Fig. 2); Discussion B. Testing
quote: Initially, integrators treat the existence of testing code in the pull request as a positive signal.
relevance: Grounds fiks's evidence-rich PR as stated-preference design; flags stated vs revealed preference gap.

title: Pull Request Decision Explained: An Empirical Overview
authors: Xunhui Zhang; Yue Yu; Georgios Gousios; Ayushi Rastogi
central_claim: 3,347,937 PRs, 95 features, 11,230 projects: same_user (submitter = integrator) is the most important factor (31% of explained variance); when CI is used, ci_failed_perc explains 18%; test_inclusion not among top factors.
cite_claim: Who submits vs who merges dominates PR decisions; the share of failed CI builds matters when CI is used.
quote: The most important factor influencing the pull request decision is same_user (with 31% variance).
relevance: Explains why self-merged agent PRs inflate C21-type rates; independent support for CI failure as a decision factor.

title: What Makes a Good Bug Report?
authors: Nicolas Bettenburg; Sascha Just; Adrian Schroeter; Cathrin Weiss; Rahul Premraj; Thomas Zimmermann [verify author list]
central_claim: Survey of Apache/Eclipse/Mozilla (466 responses; 156 developers): developers rate steps to reproduce (83%), stack traces (57%), test cases (51%) most important; reporters find test cases hardest to provide; authors recommend capture/replay tools that record test cases.
cite_claim: Developers value steps to reproduce and test cases most in bug reports, but these are hardest for reporters to supply.
quote: capture/replay tools which record test cases
relevance: Direct design precedent for fiks attaching a recorded trace and repro test to each fix.

title: Death by a thousand slops
authors: Daniel Stenberg
central_claim: About 20% of curl security-report submissions in 2025 were AI slop; about 5% were genuine vulnerabilities; maintainer considers dropping bounty rewards.
cite_claim: OSS maintainers report a rising volume of low-quality AI-generated submissions that cost review time.
quote: reduce the amount of sand in the machine
relevance: Maintainer-burden counter-argument; fiks must show its PRs are not slop (gates, evidence, rate limits).

title: QEMU Code Provenance: Use of AI-generated content
authors: QEMU project
central_claim: QEMU declines any contribution believed to include or derive from AI-generated content.
cite_claim: Some major OSS projects reject AI-generated contributions by policy, regardless of quality.
quote: will decline any contribution if use of AI is either known or suspected
relevance: Acceptance ceiling no gate can raise; limits generality of fiks's PR channel.

title: Project:Council/AI policy
authors: Gentoo Council
central_claim: Gentoo forbids contributions created with NLP AI tools (adopted 2024-04-14), citing copyright, quality and ethics.
cite_claim: Some distributions forbid AI-assisted contributions outright.
quote: expressly forbidden to contribute to Gentoo any content
relevance: Same as qemu-ai-policy: policy-based rejection.
